title: BRING IT WITH YOUR OWN HANDS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The LORD said to Moses, 'Say to the Israelites: "Anyone who brings a fellowship offering to the LORD is to bring part of it as their sacrifice to the LORD. With their own hands they are to present the food offering to the LORD; they are to bring the fat, together with the breast, and wave the breast before the LORD as a wave offering."'" - Lev 7:28-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
With their own hands.

The priest could have handled it. The worshipper could have simply delivered the animal and stepped back. But God required that the person themselves lift the offering and wave it before Him.

Faith is personal. There are things nobody can do on your behalf.

Nobody can repent for you. Nobody can believe for you. Nobody can maintain your relationship with God on your behalf — not a pastor, not a spouse, not a godly parent. You can be surrounded by faithful people and still never have lifted anything with your own hands.

The wave offering was a visible gesture — lifting the portion up and moving it outward, a physical acknowledgement that this belongs to God. It was worship you could see across the courtyard.

There is value in that. Faith that never becomes visible in any action tends to evaporate. James asks pointedly, What good is it if someone claims to have faith but has no deeds? (Jas 2:14).

What have you lifted to God with your own hands recently? Not agreed with, not admired — actually done?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I relying on other people's faith rather than exercising my own?
2. What is one thing I could do with my own hands this week as an offering to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I do not want a secondhand faith. Today I lift my own life to You with my own hands. Amen.
